A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Complexity bounds for Dirichlet process slice samplers. Their main text, algorithms, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A and B are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gaussian-mixture simulations, including runtime, effective sample size, clustering accuracy, and posterior co-clustering results in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 reports revised simulation outcomes in Section 5 and Appendix B, plus additional fixed-concentration experiments in Tables 2 and 3.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain their sampling procedures. Renaming the stick-breaking variable and explicitly specifying the occupied atoms' full conditional are notation and documentation clarifications. Fixed-alpha experiments evaluate an existing model configuration.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate univariate Gaussian-mixture clustering using balanced three-cluster and perturbed-Zipf data. The Zipf scenario changes from 500 possible labels with probabilities proportional to c^-2 to 50 labels with probabilities proportional to c^-0.5, revising the represented cluster population within the retained task.

E2.justification: The balanced-cluster study retains the same six samplers, including both slice variants, both blocked Gibbs configurations, and both CRP variants. The Zipf study retains Slice versus BGS with L=10. The fixed-alpha experiments use these corresponding comparator sets.

E3.justification: Figure 4 changes its evaluation metric from Rand index to adjusted Rand index. Appendix B.3 adds alpha=1 controls alongside the existing Gamma-prior experiments and reports both clustering metrics. The stated sample-size grids, iteration budgets, burn-in, and initialization remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.3 tests sensitivity to fixing the concentration parameter at alpha=1 in both simulation settings. Existing co-clustering and cluster-count mixing analyses remain, with revised results; no broader robustness or ablation program is introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both use iteration averages and posterior-partition boxplots; the additional tables do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The balanced-cluster runtime, ESS, and clustering plots change despite retaining their stated settings. Zipf results are replaced under the revised data distribution and, in Figure 4, a different metric. Figure 7 reverses the runtime ordering of Slice and BGS. Tables 2 and 3 add extensive fixed-alpha results, including Zipf ARI values of 0.646 for Slice and 0.352 for BGS at n=3000.

T1.justification: V2 adds Proposition 3.6 and its proof in Appendix A.6, establishing a logarithmic lower bound with positive probability under the singleton partition and ruling out a uniformly smaller-order overhead rate. Supporting Lemma A.3 is also added. Lemmas A.1 and A.2 reorganize derivations already present in v1; the earlier upper-bound results remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and principal conclusion retain the claims of posterior high-probability complexity guarantees, logarithmic slice overhead uniformly over partitions, and applicability without likelihood-specific assumptions. The new tightness result appears in Section 3 without redefining these headline claims.

C2.justification: Section 3 adds an explanation linking cluster splitting to smaller weights and narrower slice-variable supports. The conclusion redirects prospective extensions from general completely random measures toward general species-sampling processes. Existing interpretations of scalability and truncation limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: Algorithm 2 now explicitly identifies full-conditional sampling for occupied atoms, and Figure 4 newly documents thinning every two iterations; this disclosure alone does not establish that thinning changed. V2 also states that code accompanies supplementary material while retaining the same repository in a Software and data section.

R1.justification: V2 adds Canale et al. (2022) and Mena et al. (2025) to position prospective Pitman-Yor and species-sampling extensions. The broader positioning remains unchanged. The Balocchi reference is updated to its published form, rather than introducing a different work.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized language and cross-reference corrections, adds descriptive corollary titles, and organizes Appendix A into numbered proof subsections with two previously embedded derivations presented as lemmas. Software and acknowledgments headings are added; the main narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds two detailed numerical tables and revises numerous empirical displays, including Figure 4's metric, axis, and caption, other plot scales, and co-clustering panels. Typography and caption formatting change throughout, the introduction moves onto the first page, and existing figures and Table 1 are repositioned.

improvement.justification: Proposition 3.6 and Appendix A.6 resolve an important question left open in v1: the central logarithmic overhead rate is uniformly unimprovable. This substantially strengthens the theoretical characterization. Fixed-alpha controls add evidence aligned with the theory, and adjusted Rand scores make the imbalanced-clustering evaluation more informative. The revised Zipf results cannot establish same-setting performance gains, and independent-run uncertainty remains unreported.
